The "debate" around the DNC autopsy is getting silly and has been a dumb distraction for a few weeks now. That said, this is the most thorough insider account of the '24 campaign I've read, with lots of important insights. I highly recommend it.


Rob Flaherty (@Rob_Flaherty)

So, I actually talked to the DNC autopsy. 

Here’s everything I told ‘em, and more:

open.substack.com/pub/thebul…




— https://nitter.net/Rob_Flaherty/status/2054879855678804272#m

This sort of thing does not happen in a healthy democracy. We are collectively being far too quiet about all of this.


Justin J. Pearson (@Justinjpearson)

Speaker of the TN House Cameron Sexton just removed me and every Democrat — and therefore every Black elected official in the state legislature from any committee we served on.

This move strips nearly 2 million Tennesseans from the representation they deserve in TN state leg.



— https://nitter.net/Justinjpearson/status/2054317572091257198

So the GOP/Supreme Court say that Voting Rights Act protections are no longer necessary, because racism is no longer a problem, then the GOP uses the ruling to eliminate as many Black members of congress as possible. But again, racism is no longer a problem.


Jamie Dupree (@jamiedupree)

Here is the new GOP map being floated in South Carolina, which would take that state's delegation from 6-1 to 7-0 for Republicans.



— https://nitter.net/jamiedupree/status/2052474417893048809#m

If you work on, in, or around a campaign, as a staffer/consultant/vendor, you should not be betting/trading on campaign outcomes. Period.


Andrew Kaczynski (@KFILE)

The urge to insider trade on these politics markets is going to become a real problem extremely soon. Think of all the outside research/oppo firm - the number of people who know forthcoming dirt on candidates. This is not good! 

nitter.net/lukegarrett202/status/…



— https://nitter.net/KFILE/status/2052387739710980172#m
That said, I don't think there is a high degree of sophistication or insider information driving these results.

At best, the Polymarket data should be taken as a sign of where an anonymous group of people, willing to stake some amount of money, believe races stand. It's not surprising that people are bullish on Dem opportunities in November, generically they should be.

Even though this is positive for Dems and I believe we can win both races, we shouldn't be relying on Polymarket to report on who is likely to win any election.


Chris Cillizza (@ChrisCillizza)

Something is happening in Ohio this cycle.

Amy Acton ahead in gov race and Sherrod Brown ahead in Senate race.



— https://nitter.net/ChrisCillizza/status/2051694476632936866#m

A great example of what I was saying earlier this week. Money sitting in a DNC bank account may look better in FEC filings, but it does nothing to win races. It's good that they are sending it to the states where it helps win races. 
nationaljournal.com/s/731683…

The algorithm on this site will give you a skewed view of certain things, so it could just be me, but it seems like Dems (myself included) have spent way too much time  arguing about '24 and way too little sounding the alarm on the Supreme Court's latest attack on our democracy.

Ironically, if people read what the DNC did release from their post mortem, they would see that one major finding from 2024 was how much of a mistake it was for Dems to hold so much of their spending until the end, when it was too late to undo the harm the Trump campaign inflicted.

So yes, the party committee for the kleptocrat incumbent president has outraised their opponents by 17%. The difference he and others are pointing to is a cash on hand difference. Meaning - the DNC has actually been investing in winning races and in infrastructure, early.

For some reason there's been a flood of misinformation over the past 24 hours about this. In this piece, Matt Y says "The RNC has a 7 to 1 fundraising edge", which simply isn't true. Since the beginning of '25, the RNC has outraised the DNC $154 million to $132 million...

And the exact same people who were threatening civil war when a majority of VA voters approved new maps will applaud FL sneaking through maps without the public even seeing them, let alone voting on them.


John Bisognano (@johnbisognano)

The Florida Legislature is about to make all other Republican states look like beacons of transparency.

It’s 4/27 and they plan to vote on new maps TOMORROW and no member of the public has even seen a draft.

No wonder voters from all parties hate this.
flori
Fwiw Cole Allen isn't a registered Democrat, from what I can see on the voter file. Not that I think that matters, but I've seen a bunch of big accounts on this site claim otherwise.

I guarantee you that 80%+ of Dems have no idea who Hasan Piker is. This is a dumb distraction and Dems should stop taking the bait (yes, I know this is a GOP poll, which should be our first clue here).


Patrick Ruffini (@PatrickRuffini)

NEW DATA: 51% of Democrats say party leaders should denounce Hasan Piker. Less than 1 in 3 they should be in some sort of alliance with him. echeloninsights.substack.com…





— https://nitter.net/PatrickRuffini/status/2047766392745701546#m

Prepare for whiplash, as all the GOPs who were cheering on TX, then shaming CA, then threatening IN, then appalled by VA will be pivoting to cheering on FL.

Btw, if there are two states where GOPs should very much not count on Trump '24 margins to hold, it's FL and TX.


Patrick Ruffini (@PatrickRuffini)

Because Democrats have surged ahead of their pre-Texas seat count, Florida will now act to Level The Playing Field™️.



— https://nitter.net/PatrickRuffini/status/2047684662810599433#m

The TX election is in a month. This guy, who has failed at everything he's touched this year, knows he will not intimidate Thune. He's just hoping Paxton will win the runoff so he can pretend he made it happen, something that will convince exactly zero people.


ThePersistence (@ScottPresler)

Senate Majority Leader Thune has 8 days — until the end of April — to pass the SAVE America Act 

before I actively get involved in the primaries in Louisiana & Texas. 

🗓️ May 16: LA
🗓️ May 26: TX

CC

So I guess we're to believe the conservatives in VA just got fired up about this issue one day too late?


Jason Miyares (@JasonMiyaresVA)

Yesterday’s results will prove to be a pyrrhic victory for Democrats in Virginia.

The raw anger is palpable and now Abigail Spanberger, Don Scott, Louise Lucas, and the rest of the Richmond Democrats will own this.

Governor Spanberger lied to voters and they won’t easily forget that. Now every insane leftist bill/vote by the radicals that will emerge from

The downstream effect of the election denialism that has become mainstream under MAGA is people like this guy making conspiracy theory videos about the cadence by which counties always have released their vote counts. We're all dumber for it.


RigoStaRR (@RigoIrizarry)

Virginia something isn’t adding up! How do you jump 64,000 votes in just a five minutes? Make it make sense

Video
  





— https://nitter.net/RigoIrizarry/status/2046781431221727296#m

Shameless personal plug: are any of my Capitol Hill/campaign/advocacy folks interviewing for interns? My daughter is finishing her freshman year at UMD, has experience with campaign and official office internships in the MD legislature (and has even testified before the MD Senate!).
There's nothing in here they wouldn't already know.

Of course, the voters in this special election were overwhelmingly regular voters in previous elections, But, among those who didn't vote in the 2022 midterm election, they were +19 women (ie, almost 60% of those surge voters) and +22 Dem.
Another interesting component of turnout, in the special election the overall turnout was +8 women, whereas in the 2024 general that saw Trump carry the district the turnout was +6 women.

In '24, in terms of party reg, the electorate was +7 GOP. In this special, the electorate was just +1 GOP, demonstrating a clear turnout advantage for Dems, but also meaning that the 22 point swing was driven by both persuasion and turnout advantages, with more of the swing coming from persuasion.

According to Ballotpedia, Drey's campaign emphasized education funding, bodily autonomy, childcare, and economic mobility, while her GOP opponent campaigned on eliminating the state income tax, border security, and anti abortion policies. ballotpedia.org/Iowa_State_S...
According to this post from the NEA, the Drey campaign knocked on roughly 170,000 doors in the district, and made 30,000 phone calls. www.nea.org/nea-today/al...

This election happened in August of last year, in a district that Trump carried by 11 pts in 2024. The Dem candidate, Catelin Drey, won by an almost identical margin, representing an almost 22 pt swing towards Dems, resulting in GOPs losing their supermajority in the IA Senate.

I've lagged on my intention to sporadically share data, when we get it, on recent special elections where we've seen large swings to Dems, looking under the head in an effort to get a sense of what drove these results and what they might mean for November. Back at it - IASD01.

Join us for "It's the Democracy, Stupid" today at 1pm ET! @eisendrath.net is joined by veteran Democratic strategist  @tbonier.bsky.social to discuss data, democracy and what the midterms look like for Democrats and more. Subscribe for free to watch:
open.substack.com/live-stream/...

Not every vote is in (the outlined counties don't have >95% counted, and Maverick hasn't reported at all), but this shows the swing between Harris' margin in '24 and the Dem margin in yesterday's primary turnout. You can see in south Texas the shifts were >100%.
Let's keep in mind, the GOP reportedly spent upwards of $80 million on their primaries in Texas, well more than double the amount spent by Dems.
Here are 4 districts the TX GOP gerrymandered to gain seats in November, with the Dem and GOP primary vote. Dems outvoted GOPs in every one of them.

Wow, the Dem primary turnout among Hispanic voters in Texas is going to be giving the GOP sweats for the next 8 months. 

Take Zapata County - turnout in the Dem primary there yesterday was 143% the total number of votes Harris won in the 2024 general election. That's wild.
There are only 348 voters in the cell so I wouldn’t read too much into it.
Here's a better version with it sorted by partisanship gaps, and with the N size included for each group

Some notes:
- Black women are leading the way with the biggest Dem advantage across every age group
- Black men are also showing huge Dem margins
- Dems lead in every single group of under age 30 voters, even white men
- GOPs don't have an advantage with any group <50

I made this monster of a chart to show the partisan split of the early/abs vote in the TX primary by age/race/gender. 

You can see why Republicans must be worried about what they're seeing in the turnout data.

A short thread on letting go of Zombie, pre-Trump 2025-2026 understanding of politics......

We are in a new era.  Strategists must stay close to the events of today, to the data in front of us, and not bring old understandings to cloud or hamper with what must be done now.  1/
